summary: Configured node1 so only root and opsadmin may schedule cron jobs. The policy and crond service persisted across a verified node restart.
actions_performed: Created /etc/cron.allow containing exactly root and opsadmin.
Set /etc/cron.allow ownership to root:root and permissions to 0600.
Verified root and opsadmin pass cron access control while the unlisted antrieb user is denied.
Restarted node1 safely and verified a changed boot identity, full system recovery, active/enabled crond, and persistent access controls.

evidence.requirement: Only root and opsadmin can schedule cron jobs on node1
evidence.summary: Shows the exact two-entry allow file, secure ownership and mode, successful access-gate behavior for root and opsadmin, denial for unlisted antrieb, and active crond before and after restart.

Captures healthy pre-restart state and acknowledgement, then proves the boot ID changed from 2fc81aed-3ce8-4a35-8f4c-b73206afa45f to 027ba6a0-7266-416f-8357-741c3238bea0, followed by recovered system, crond, account, policy, and access behavior.
